description:
A user program can reach a Rust panic by passing a value whose static type is any to an extern with a typed parameter.

Program (develop 8f63dd600):

extern "C" defp fz_op_add_ii(integer, integer) :: integer,
  raises: ArithmeticError,
  message: "bad argument in arithmetic expression"

def main() do
  send(self(), 1.5)
  receive do
    x -> dbg(fz_op_add_ii(x, 1))
  end
end

Observed:
- fz2 interp: stops with the host message 'fz2 interp: extern integer arg must be Int'.
- fz2 run and the built binary: 'thread caused non-unwinding panic. aborting.' with fz_unbox_int (runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:217) on the stack.

When the argument's static type is narrower than any and outside the parameter's type, the compiler already refuses the call with error[spec/violation] (for example an argument typed float | :atom). The hole is the any case: the call is admitted and the wrapper unboxes without a check that can fail in Fz terms.

Expected: all three paths end the process with the same Fz error for the argument (Elixir's shape for the equivalent is an ArgumentError / ArithmeticError raised at the call), catchable by rescue, with no Rust panic and no host-only message.

Fails before, passes after: a fixture with the program above and expect: abort with the Fz error on stderr, three paths; a second fixture that rescues it.

Acceptance: full gate green.
title: A value of the wrong kind passed to a typed extern is a Fz error, not a host panic
